slides.texte_overlay:
How to master the
art of small talk
Have three easy openers ready. "How's your week going?", "What brings you here?", "Any plans for the weekend?" Knowing your first line takes away half the nerves before you start.
Answer with a bit more than needed. Not just "Good." Try "Good, I finally tried that new ramen place." One extra detail gives the other person something to grab and ask about.
Notice something and say it. "Nice jacket, where's it from?" or "This place is packed tonight." Simple observations feel natural and give the chat an easy, relaxed start.
Keep a few fresh topics in your pocket. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I always have something light and interesting to bring up with anyone.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I always have something light and interesting to bring up when small talk stalls.

slides.texte_overlay: Use the weekend bridge. Ask about last weekend early in the week and next weekend later on. It's the easiest topic in the world, and it often leads to the person's real passions.
Mirror a word they used. They say "crazy week", you ask "Crazy how?" Repeating their own words shows you're listening and invites them to open up without any effort.
Know when to wrap it up. "Great catching up, see you around." Small talk is meant to be small. Ending it while it's still pleasant makes people happy to talk to you again next time.
